# v1.0.10 — the benchmark behind 57.3%

The Results compare observed reversion in the 50-64 band against a no-change benchmark: 63.7%
observed, **57.3% expected** under the 2025 age-specific cut-offs. That expectation had no archived
generator. `96_stratum_bench.R` runs the same model at the AWGS 2019 cut-offs only, and the manifest
pointed Table S27 at it, so a reader following the manifest could reproduce the observed value but
not the benchmark beside it.

## What changed

- `code/charls_only/99_stratum_bench_2025.R` runs the no-change model of `96_stratum_bench.R` with
  the 2025 cut-offs. The generative model, the calibration and the error term are unchanged; only
  the cut-offs and the classification differ, and the three 2019 rows are kept as a check that the
  two scripts agree (59.5%, 67.8%, 52.1%).
  - `50-64, 2025`: 433 of 3,213 readings low; observed 63.7%; expected **57.3%**
    (95% simulation interval 42.9-71.8); observed/expected 1.11.
- `manifest/s27/JFA_stratum_bench_2025.csv` archives the seven rows of that run. The script
  reproduces the file byte for byte; no respondent-level data are in it.
- `manifest/outputs.csv` now maps Table S27 to `95_rev31_age.R + 96_stratum_bench.R + 99_stratum_bench_2025.R`
  and records the new output file.
- The 2025 classification itself was already in the package: `code/01_build.R` builds `low11_25`
  and `low13_25` (below 34 and 20 kg at 50-64 years, below 28 and 18 kg above). The script therefore
  reads `out/jamda_full.rds` and nothing else; there is no machine-specific path, and a different
  analysis directory can be named once with `CHARLS_ANALYSIS_DIR`.

## What did not change

No estimate in the manuscript changed. The 57.3% was already in the submitted text; this release
adds the code that produces it.

## Known remaining gap

`manifest/outputs.csv` still has no row for Tables S29-S31 and S33-S36. Scripts that plausibly
produce them are in `code/`, but none names the table in its header, and a guessed mapping would
repeat the error this release corrects.

Cite this version, or the concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.23677282`, which resolves here. Versions
1.0.8 and 1.0.9 remain citable at their own version DOIs.
